title: Meter Services Standard — Estimated Reads, True-Ups and Verification Re-Reads on the Utility Pass-Through Service
content:
This standard governs Utility Pass-Through Service cycles billed without a regular actual read, the read that follows them, and unusually high actual water reads.

## Retired clause

The former clause "When a submeter cannot be read on the read day, the cycle is billed on an estimated read set at the average daily consumption of the schedule's number of most recent actual-read billing periods (their total consumption divided by the total days they cover) times the days in the cycle" is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for estimating a water read.

## Clauses in force

**A. Limit on consecutive estimates.** No more than the schedule's maximum number of consecutive cycles may be billed on estimates, counting the run of consecutive billing periods, ending with the most recent one, whose billed read for that service is an estimated read. The next cycle must be billed on an actual read, arranged with the resident if access is the obstacle.

**B. True-up on the first actual read.** The first actual read after one or more estimates is billed against the last estimated register reading, which trues up cumulative use. When the actual register reading is below the last estimated one, the over-estimated consumption is credited at the rates of the periods it was billed in, as an estimated-read true-up credit, and the cycle's consumption is billed as zero.

**C. High-bill verification re-read.** When an actual water read shows consumption above the schedule's high-bill re-read threshold percent of the baseline consumption, the meter is re-read before the statement is issued, and the statement bills the verification re-read.

**Baseline consumption** means the average water consumption of the actual or verification re-read water reads over the schedule's number of leak-adjustment baseline periods — the billing periods immediately before the period in question that were billed on an actual (not estimated) water read — rounded to two decimals.

## Cases (hypothetical readings)

| Case | Facts | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Estimate run at the limit | Limit 2; the last two cycles were billed on estimated reads | The next cycle must be billed on an actual read |
| Actual read above last estimate | Last estimated register reading 1,250.40; actual register reading 1,256.00 | The cycle bills 5.60 kgal, measured from 1,250.40 |
| Actual read below last estimate | Last estimated register reading 1,250.40; actual register reading 1,248.10 | The 2.30 kgal over-estimated is credited at the rates of the periods it was billed in; the cycle's consumption is billed as zero |
| High actual read | Baseline 4.00 kgal; threshold 150 percent, so 6.00 kgal; actual read 6.40 kgal | Above 6.00: the meter is re-read before the statement and the statement bills the re-read |
| Actual read at the threshold | Baseline 4.00 kgal; actual read exactly 6.00 kgal | Not above the threshold; no re-read is required by clause C |

## Basis Q&A

**Is the over-estimate credited at today's rates?** No — at the rates of the periods in which it was billed.

**Which reads make up the baseline consumption?** The actual or verification re-read water reads of the baseline periods, which are the billing periods immediately before the period in question that were billed on an actual water read; periods billed on an estimated read are not among them.

superseded_clauses: When a submeter cannot be read on the read day, the cycle is billed on an estimated read set at utility_msr_estimate_daily_use times the days in the cycle.
